claims.text: An actively learned NNIP trained on ab initio solid and liquid configurations will improve phase-space overlap with the target DFT landscape relative to an EAM reference.
The NNIP intervention will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by at least 50% relative to the EAM references used in TOR-TILD.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi is a representative multicomponent high-entropy alloy for studying disordered solids and liquids near melting.
Force matching and energy fitting to ab initio data can be used to construct the proposed NNIP reference.
An active-learning loop can identify and add high-error configurations to the NNIP training set.
Iteratively adding high-error configurations will ensure full coverage of the diverse solid and liquid phase space.
The proposed method is applicable over approximately 0.9–1.1 times the melting temperature of multicomponent HEAs.
Pure Ni, pure Cu, and Ni-Cu mixtures provide relevant elemental or binary benchmarks for the method.
The NNIP can capture complex many-body interactions and local structural motifs in the high-temperature HEA.
The NNIP can serve as an enhanced configuration generator for reference-to-DFT free-energy mapping.
Training on an extensive, iteratively refined ab initio dataset enables the NNIP to reproduce the variety of local configurations in high-temperature disordered states.
Improved representation of local configurations increases phase-space overlap between the NNIP reference and the DFT target.
Increased reference-target phase-space overlap reduces thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
Reduced integration-path mismatch will yield more reliable free-energy estimates with lower statistical error.
Traditional EAM references used in TOR-TILD have poor phase-space overlap with ab initio liquid configurations.
The method should remain robust for systems with chemical complexity similar to CoCrFeMnNi within the specified temperature range.
Performance may deteriorate for substantially different compositions, temperature regimes, or configurational dynamics.
Underrepresentation of configurational-space regions may limit the improvement obtained from active learning.
